lock_payload_format_1_legacy.company_id: 0x5E01 (0x015E byte-swapped — firmware quirk; filter for both)

advertising.notes: Two advertisers exist. The LOCK advertises its per-lock UUID in manufacturer data (see `identification`). The CONTROLLER (phone role) must advertise legacy-connectable at ~250 ms interval (400 x 0.625 ms), lowest TX power, company ID 0x015E, payload of TLV-ish records: default [0x05 + 6 fresh random bytes] (anti-replay freshness beacon, new randomness per advert), optional [0x04, antennaOffset] (RSSI calibration), slow mode [0x01,0x14,0,0,0].

connection.roles: INVERTED: the lock is central + GATT client; the controller is peripheral + GATT server + advertiser. The controller never connects to the lock — it advertises and answers. (The phone app additionally scans for lock adverts for presence/proximity, but all bulk data flows over the phone-hosted service.)

auth.notes: Authenticated REST (e.g. PUT /Users/{userId}/Locks/{lockId}/Commands with body {"command":<int>,"deviceStates":[...]}) plus a per-user WebSocket. Recorded for history only — the service is dead.

data_leaves_device: lock/unlock commands and lock state (via the Kevo Plus gateway relay)

endpoints.returns: Remote lock/unlock relay via the Kevo Plus gateway (GatewayCommandType: LOCK=1, UNLOCK=2, BOLT_POSITION_QUERY=4, DEVICE_STATE_UPDATE=5, DEVICE_STATE_QUERY=6, TIME_SYNC=8, QUERY_HISTORY=16)

cloud.failure_mode: Already happened: ASSA ABLOY shut down the Kevo app and web portal on 2025-11-14. Remote lock/unlock, eKey management, lock history and Kevo Plus gateway relay all stopped (every gateway command transited this cloud — the app even surfaced literal '504 - Gateway timeout' strings when the relay failed). Local BLE control, the physical key and key fobs are unaffected. UniKey (a separate company) has offered continued service to customers; local operation does not depend on it.

device.name: Kwikset Kevo
device.notes:
Touch-to-open smart deadbolt built on UniKey's BLE platform. ASSA ABLOY shut down the Kevo app and web portal on 2025-11-14 (confirmed against kwikset.com and ca.weiserlock.com support notices); the physical key and key fobs still work, which proves the lock-side BLE auth is fully self-contained. Local BLE is now the only electronic control path.
INVERTED BLE ROLES — the single most important fact about this device: the LOCK is the BLE central and GATT client. It scans, connects, and drives the session with reads and writes. The phone (or fob, or a local controller) is the PERIPHERAL: it advertises manufacturer data under company ID 0x015E and HOSTS the single GATT service listed below. There are no NOTIFY characteristics; phone-to-lock data rides GATT read responses because the lock polls. A local controller must therefore run as a BLE peripheral with a GATT server (Linux BlueZ supports this), not as the usual scanning central. This is why the Android app required Android 5.0+ (first release with peripheral mode).
Security is entirely application-layer: no BLE pairing/bonding, no link-layer encryption (per NCC Group's 2022 advisory). Authentication is an HMAC-SHA256 challenge-response over a per-lock shared secret derived from X25519 ECDH during enrollment.
There is NO WiFi/LAN protocol anywhere in the system (full-decompile sweep: no DatagramSocket/MulticastSocket/NsdManager/WifiManager use in com.unikey.*). The Kevo Plus gateway (RPU) is wired Ethernet + BLE only; every gateway command historically transited the UniKey cloud. Its vendor-documented "Local Debug" ports (TCP 499/11000) appear nowhere in the app and have never been publicly investigated — the most interesting unexplored local surface.
Research status: phone-side protocol fully mapped from the decompiled APK (service/characteristic UUIDs, properties, opcodes, advertisement format, HMAC construction, secret derivation, enrollment state machines, absence of LAN code all re-verified in v3.1.1.33967p). Lock-side firmware behaviour, TLV certificate field names, LIC/time-sync layout and the trailing bytes of the lock advertisement need one over-the-air capture (no link-layer encryption, so any LE sniffer works).

issued_to_client: Session certificate written by the lock at enroll (TLV field set recovered from use sites)
Shared secret, derived independently on both sides, never transmitted
credentials.notes: No WiFi exists anywhere in the system. Certificates are UniKey TLV records [field:1][len:2 LE][value]; known fields include 0x30=role, 0x32=UUID, 0x35=X25519 public key, 0x36=Ed25519 public key, 0xB7=expiry, 0x14=issued-at, 0x11=cert type. Field names were compile-time-stripped; numeric tags recovered from use sites.
stored_on_device: Per-client session certificates (UniKey TLV certs) and the derived shared secrets
Own X25519/Ed25519 identity keypairs (issued at manufacture)

factory_reset.effect: A reset exists (Kwikset support documents holding the interior "A" button for ~20 s on 2nd-gen; 1st-gen differs) and clears enrolled devices, after which every phone/fob must re-enroll. The exact per-generation procedure is documented by the vendor, not established here — a guessed sequence on a door lock can leave someone locked out of their home.

ble.notes: No BLE link-layer pairing at all — enrollment is the application-layer certificate exchange below. The controller must advertise company ID 0x015E with the freshness-beacon payload (see `advertising`) and host the GATT service before the lock is put into enroll mode.

methods.description: Tap-to-enroll: the phone (or local controller) advertises as a peripheral; the user touches the lock's interior program/enroll control to make the lock scan and connect; certs and nonces are exchanged over the phone-hosted GATT service and both sides derive the shared secret. Command opcode 0x15 (tap-to-enroll) starts it.

steps.action: Advertise as a BLE peripheral (company 0x015E, payload [0x05 + 6 fresh random bytes]) and host the GATT service 86130247-E942-4FE5-AA46-E30768A0C1B0 with its four characteristics.
Put the lock into enroll mode (physical control on the lock's interior unit; the vendor flow pairs this with touching the lock — 'tap-to-enroll').
steps.expect: The lock scans for company-0x015E adverts and connects to the controller.

steps.action: Answer the enroll exchange driven by the lock via the COMMAND characteristic: device public cert (0x29), server public cert (0x28), phone 32-byte nonce (0x40); receive lock hardware cert (0x21), manufacturer cert chain (0x22), lock nonce (0x43) and the session certificate (0x60).
steps.expect: Lock writes the session certificate; STATUS ack 0x60 marks enroll success.

steps.action: Derive and cache the shared secret: HMAC-SHA256(key = X25519(own private key, lock X25519 public key from certificate field 0x35), msg = lockNonce || phoneNonce), both nonces exactly 32 bytes.

setup.notes: The lock only answers HMAC challenge-responses keyed by a per-lock shared secret, and that secret only comes into existence during an enrollment exchange — so yes, provisioning is genuinely required. Two routes exist: (a) extract the per-lock shared secret and device certificate from a phone that was paired while the app still worked (SharedPreferences `device_shared_secret` entries plus the sqlcipher `kevo` database; the DB key is wrapped by an Android-Keystore RSA key, so extraction needs the phone itself), or (b) self-enroll: implement the tap-to-enroll exchange below from your own controller — it is purely lock<->phone and needs no cloud (the official app registers the new eKey to the cloud afterwards, but that step is irrelevant to local operation; whether the lock later de-auths devices that never appear in the cloud is UNKNOWN and needs a capture). Confidence is medium: the full exchange is read out of the decompiled app but has not been run against hardware here.

rejoin.notes: A previously enrolled client rejoins with its cached shared secret (or re-runs the key-present flow with its device/permission certificates if the cache was wiped — STATUS verdict 0xF0 forces exactly that). A reset is only needed to revoke a lost credential.

model_detection.notes: The LOCK advertises manufacturer data with its per-lock 16-byte UUID (the same lockId the cloud API used). Format 2 (21 bytes): [0x02][16-byte UUID big-endian][u32 little-endian] under company 0x015E. Format 1 legacy (17 bytes): [16-byte UUID][u8] under company 0x5E01 — the same ID byte-swapped on the wire, a firmware quirk the app filters for explicitly. A wildcard filter on company 0x015E finds any lock (the app's admin/enroll scan). The trailing u32/u8 semantics are unknown (status/counter?) — capture item.

covers: lock / unlock / toggle / bolt-position query / battery level over local BLE, with no cloud involved
tap-to-enroll of new controllers (lock<->phone exchange only)
lock history pull (opcode 0x19) and firmware update transport (opcode 0x9B) over BLE
not_covered: remote access (was cloud + Kevo Plus gateway relay; the gateway has no documented LAN API — its 'Local Debug' ports TCP 499/11000 are unexplored)
lock-side behaviour confirmation — no over-the-air capture has been made yet
time sync / scheduled eKeys fidelity (Lock Information Certificate layout unknown — capture item)

firmware_upgrade.advanced_reason: Writes lock firmware. A failed or wrong image can brick the lock, and the image format/signing is not understood — the app treats it as an opaque blob. Recovery path is unknown; do not use until a capture documents the real flow.
firmware_upgrade.description: Begin firmware upgrade (command value [version LE..., 0x9B]). Two transports: legacy DATA_STREAM (header -> ack 0x97; 256-byte chunks -> ack 0x98 with next offset u24 LE; per-block [len u16][CRC16] -> ack 0x9D; 0x9E = image verified) or UPC (900-byte chunks inside signed certs; next offset in result field 0x9B). Image signing is opaque to the app — lock-side.
firmware_upgrade.name: firmwareUpgradeCommand

lock_history.description: Request lock event history (uploaded to cloud in the official app; usable locally)
lock_history.name: LockHistoryCommand

tap_to_enroll.description: Tap-to-enroll a new authorized device (locks and Kevo Plus gateway; gateway enrolls as hardware type 19 / product descriptor RPU1)
tap_to_enroll.name: tapToEnrollCommand

toggle.direction: client_to_device (read by lock from COMMAND characteristic)
toggle.name: KevoLockToggleCommand

crypto.challenge_response: resp = HMAC-SHA256(key = sharedSecret, msg = nonce XOR cmd) — the 4-byte pending command is XORed into nonce bytes 0..3, then HMACed (DeviceChallengeResponseProtocolMachineDelegateImpl.calculateHmac, JCA HmacSHA256). The 32-byte result is left in DATA_STREAM for the lock to read.
crypto.implementation: 100% pure Java (JCA + vendored Tink X25519/Ed25519) — no native code
crypto.shared_secret_derivation: At enroll/first contact: secret = HMAC-SHA256(key = X25519(phonePriv, lockPub from certificate field 0x35), msg = lockNonce || phoneNonce), both nonces exactly 32 bytes (Secret.Builder / CryptoDelegate). Key-present (server-provisioned) route: the phone AES-128-CBC-decrypts the permission's server-encrypted secret with key = X25519(serverPub, phonePriv).

enroll_exchange.description: Tap-to-enroll (DeviceTapToEnrollProtocolMachineImpl): creates a brand-new authorized device, lock<->phone only. Phone command bytes -> steps: 0x29 device public cert (lock reads phone; acks STATUS 0x21/0x22, validity 0x24), 0x28 server public cert (acks 0x21/0x22), 0x40 phone 32-byte nonce (ack 0x40), 0x21 lock hardware cert (lock writes; ack 0x21), 0x22 lock manufacturer cert chain (ack 0x22), 0x43 lock 32-byte nonce (ack 0x42), 0x60 session certificate (lock writes; ack 0x60 = enroll success). The phone's own cert is generated once (random UUID + 32-byte seed -> X25519 + Ed25519 keypairs) as a UniKey TLV cert.
enroll_exchange.verification: confirmed (state machine read from the APK; not executed against a lock)

crc.notes: Used per firmware-image block during BLE firmware update ([len u16][CRC16] per block). Not a general message CRC.

framing.notes: Lock UUID and device UUID travel big-endian; multi-byte lengths inside TLV certs are little-endian; the firmware version command carries the version little-endian. Certificate TLV: [field:1][len:2 LE][value].

TLV certificate field names (compile-time-stripped; numeric tags recovered from use sites)
LIC / timing-cert layout for time sync
Trailing u32/u8 semantics in the lock advertisement

session_flow.battery_reporting: Byte[1] of the 0x04 verdict STATUS; no separate battery opcode.
session_flow.description:
Normal touch-to-open / lock / unlock session, all driven by the lock as GATT client (DeviceConnectionProtocolMachineImpl + DeviceChallengeResponseProtocolMachineImpl): 1. Lock writes STATUS [0,0,0,0x01] — challenge-UUID begin. 2. Lock reads DATA_STREAM <- phone's 16-byte device UUID (BE). 3. Lock writes DATA_STREAM -> its 16-byte lock UUID (fragment-tolerant). 4. Lock writes STATUS [1,x,x,0x01] — complete; phone resolves/creates
   the shared secret for that lock UUID (cached, else key-present flow).
5. Lock reads COMMAND <- phone's pending [0,0,0,opcode]. 6. Lock writes STATUS [x,x,lockState,0x02] — nonce challenge start. 7. Lock writes DATA_STREAM -> 32-byte nonce. 8. Lock writes STATUS [...,0x03] — HMAC request. 9. Lock reads DATA_STREAM <- 32-byte HMAC (see crypto.challenge_response). 10. Lock writes STATUS [result,battery,x,0x04] — verdict: 0x01 accepted
    (byte[1] = battery level); 0xF0 denied AND the phone wipes its
    cached secret, forcing the key-present flow next time.
session_flow.verification: confirmed (from decompiled state machines; not yet replayed against hardware)

characteristics.description: READ (phone side). The lock reads the phone's pending 4-byte command [0,0,0,opcode]; the controller updates this value between polls. See `protocol.commands` for opcodes.
characteristics.name: UNIKEY_CHAR_COMMAND

characteristics.description: READ+WRITE (phone side). Bulk data: device UUIDs, nonces, HMAC responses, firmware chunks. The lock both reads (phone's UUID, 32-byte HMAC) and writes (lock UUID, 32-byte nonce) here, with fragment-tolerant concatenation.
characteristics.name: UNIKEY_CHAR_DATA_STREAM

characteristics.description: WRITE (phone side). The lock writes 4-byte flow-control/status messages; dispatch is on byte[3]. Values seen in the state machines: 0x01 challenge-UUID begin/complete, 0x02 nonce challenge start (byte[2] carries lock state), 0x03 HMAC request, 0x04 verdict (byte[0] result: 0x01 accepted / 0xF0 denied-and-wipe; byte[1] battery), 0x9A firmware version ([patch,minor,major]), 0x9B firmware-upgrade marker, 0x12 bolt-position family, 0x15 enroll begin result, 0x30 key-present begin. Enroll/key-present acks: 0x21/0x22/0x24/0x31/0x38/0x40/0x42/0x43/0x60.
characteristics.name: UNIKEY_CHAR_STATUS

characteristics.description: READ+WRITE (phone side). UniKey TLV "certificate" channel (UPC): enrollment, settings, history, firmware, result codes. Post-auth certs are HMAC-signed: field 0x22 = HMAC-SHA256(sharedSecret, serializedCert XOR nonce); nonces rotate every connection so captured certs do not replay. Result certs carry field 0xBD result codes (1=SUCCESS, 2=CONTINUE, 3=UNINITIALIZED, 4=COMMAND_TIMEOUT, 0=FAILURE, -1=FAILURE_SLEEPING, -3=FAILURE_BAD_UDATA, -4=FAILURE_GATT, -5=FAILURE_NO_OWNER, -6=FAILURE_RESOURCES, -7=PROTOCOL_ERROR, -8=FAILURE_DOOR_OPEN, -9=FAILURE_IR, -10=FAILURE_BAD_DATA, -11=FAILURE_HAS_OWNER, -12=FAILURE_LOW_BATT, -13=INVALID_CERTIFICATE, -14=FAILURE_RANGE, -15=FAILURE_INSIDE, -16=UNAUTHORIZED).
characteristics.name: UNIKEY_CHAR_CERTIFICATE

services.description: The only GATT service in the system, and it lives on the CLIENT side — the lock connects to it as GATT client. No NOTIFY characteristics anywhere: the lock polls. A fifth characteristic 0x0969 is constructed in the app's static initializer but never added to the service — dead code, recorded here so nobody chases it.
services.name: UniKey Device Service (hosted by the phone/controller)
